description: This topic covers the two main Islamic festivals (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha), the Hijri calendar and its months, the sacred months, the Friday (Jumua) prayer, voluntary fasting, and the social importance of communal Islamic practices.

mcq.questionText: Which festival marks the end of the month of fasting, Ramadan?
mcq.explanation: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawwal, immediately after the completion of fasting in Ramadan.

mcq.questionText: Eid al-Adha is also known as the festival of which act?
mcq.explanation: Eid al-Adha is called the Festival of Sacrifice, commemorating Prophet Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah.

mcq.questionText: In which month of the Islamic calendar is Eid al-Adha celebrated?
mcq.explanation: Eid al-Adha falls on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, during the season of the Hajj pilgrimage.

mcq.questionText: How many months are there in the Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
mcq.explanation: The Islamic calendar has twelve lunar months, each beginning with the sighting of the new moon.

mcq.questionText: The Islamic calendar is based on the cycles of which heavenly body?
mcq.explanation: The Hijri calendar is lunar, with each month determined by the phases of the moon.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the first month of the Islamic calendar?
mcq.explanation: Muharram is the first month of the Hijri year and is one of the four sacred months.

mcq.questionText: The special congregational prayer held every week on Friday is called:
mcq.explanation: Salat al-Jumua is the Friday congregational prayer that replaces the normal Dhuhr prayer for Muslims attending the mosque.

mcq.questionText: How many sacred (forbidden) months are there in the Islamic calendar?
mcq.explanation: There are four sacred months: Dhul-Qi'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram and Rajab, during which fighting was traditionally forbidden.

mcq.questionText: A key part of the Jumua prayer that is not found in ordinary daily prayers is the:
mcq.explanation: The Friday prayer includes a khutbah (sermon) delivered by the imam before the two units of prayer.

mcq.questionText: On the morning of both Eids, Muslims gather to perform a special prayer called:
mcq.explanation: Salat al-Eid is a special congregational prayer performed in the morning on both Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.

mcq.questionText: Which charity is given by Muslims before the Eid al-Fitr prayer to help the poor share in the celebration?
mcq.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is an obligatory charity given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer so that the needy can also enjoy the festival.

mcq.questionText: The voluntary fast that many Muslims observe each week is usually kept on which two days?
mcq.explanation: Fasting on Mondays and Thursdays is a recommended voluntary practice that the Prophet Muhammad regularly observed.

mcq.questionText: The animal slaughtered during Eid al-Adha as an act of worship is known as the:
mcq.explanation: Udhiyah, also called Qurbani, is the sacrificial animal whose meat is shared among family, friends and the poor.

mcq.questionText: From which historic event does the Islamic calendar count its years (Year 1)?

options.text: The birth of the Prophet Muhammad
The first revelation of the Qur'an
The migration (Hijra) from Makkah to Madinah

mcq.explanation: The Hijri calendar begins counting from the year of the Hijra, the Prophet's migration from Makkah to Madinah.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is a true social benefit of communal practices such as Jumua and the Eid prayers?

options.text: They divide the rich from the poor
They strengthen unity and brotherhood among Muslims
They are only for adult men with no benefit to society
They replace the need for daily prayers

mcq.explanation: Gathering for Jumua and Eid brings Muslims of all backgrounds together, building unity, brotherhood and care for one another.

fib.questionText: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of the month of _____.
fib.explanation: Shawwal is the month that follows Ramadan, and Eid al-Fitr begins on its first day.

fib.questionText: Eid al-Adha commemorates the willingness of Prophet _____ to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah.
fib.explanation: Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) showed complete submission to Allah, and this act is remembered during Eid al-Adha.

fib.questionText: The Islamic calendar is also called the _____ calendar, named after the migration of the Prophet.
fib.explanation: The word Hijri comes from Hijra, the migration from Makkah to Madinah, which marks year one of the calendar.

fib.questionText: The month in which Muslims fast from dawn to sunset every year is called _____.
fib.explanation: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar and the month of obligatory fasting.

fib.questionText: The sermon delivered before the Friday prayer is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The khutbah is the address given by the imam, reminding the congregation about faith and good conduct.

fib.questionText: The Friday congregational prayer takes the place of the _____ prayer for those who attend.
fib.explanation: Salat al-Jumua is prayed instead of the midday Dhuhr prayer on Fridays.

fib.questionText: Eid al-Adha is celebrated on the tenth day of the month of _____.
fib.explanation: Dhul-Hijjah is the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar and the month of the Hajj pilgrimage.

fib.questionText: The charity given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer to help the needy is called Zakat al-_____.
fib.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid prayer so the poor can also celebrate the festival.

fib.questionText: Because it is shorter than the solar year, the Islamic lunar year has about 354 _____.
fib.explanation: The lunar year is roughly 11 days shorter than the solar year, so Islamic months shift earlier each year.

fib.questionText: Voluntary fasting that is not obligatory is often described as _____ fasting.
fib.explanation: Sunnah (or recommended) fasts, such as those on Mondays and Thursdays, earn reward but are not compulsory.

tf.questionText: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated immediately after the month of Ramadan.
tf.explanation: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan and begins on the first day of Shawwal.

tf.questionText: The Islamic calendar follows the movement of the sun rather than the moon.
tf.explanation: The Islamic calendar is lunar; its months are based on the phases of the moon.

tf.questionText: There are four sacred months in the Islamic calendar.
tf.explanation: The four sacred months are Dhul-Qi'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram and Rajab.

tf.questionText: The Friday prayer (Jumua) includes a sermon delivered by the imam.
tf.explanation: The khutbah (sermon) is an essential part of the Jumua prayer.

tf.questionText: Eid al-Adha takes place during the season of the Hajj pilgrimage.
tf.explanation: Eid al-Adha falls on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, the same month in which Hajj is performed.

tf.questionText: Muslims are only allowed to fast during the month of Ramadan and at no other time.
tf.explanation: Besides Ramadan, Muslims may keep voluntary fasts such as Mondays and Thursdays and other recommended days.

tf.questionText: Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer to help the poor.
tf.explanation: This charity ensures that even the needy can take part in the joy of Eid.

tf.questionText: The Islamic year begins with the month of Ramadan.
tf.explanation: The first month of the Islamic calendar is Muharram, not Ramadan.

tf.questionText: The meat from the Eid al-Adha sacrifice is meant to be shared with family, friends and the poor.
tf.explanation: Sharing the sacrificial meat is part of the festival and strengthens care for the community.

tf.questionText: The Islamic lunar year is longer than the Western solar year.
tf.explanation: The lunar year is about 11 days shorter than the solar year, so Islamic dates move earlier each year.

hoq.questionText: Why do the dates of Ramadan and the two Eids move to an earlier point in the Western (solar) year as the years pass?

options.text: Because the lunar year is about 11 days shorter than the solar year
Because Muslims change the dates each year by choice
Because the solar year has no fixed length
Because leap years are added to Ramadan

hoq.explanation: Since the lunar year is roughly 11 days shorter than the solar year, Islamic dates shift earlier in the Gregorian calendar each year.

hoq.questionText: How does giving Zakat al-Fitr before the Eid prayer reflect the social purpose of Islamic festivals?

options.text: It rewards only the wealthy for their savings
It ensures the poor can also enjoy the festival, promoting equality and compassion
It is a payment to avoid attending the Eid prayer
It replaces the obligation of the Eid prayer

hoq.explanation: By giving before the prayer, the community ensures even the needy can celebrate, showing the festival's emphasis on compassion and social unity.

hoq.questionText: What does the weekly gathering for Jumua prayer best teach Muslims about their faith?

options.text: That worship is a private matter only
That prayer is unnecessary on other days
That Islam values regular community gathering, learning and unity
That only the imam needs to worship

hoq.explanation: Jumua brings Muslims together each week to pray, hear guidance in the khutbah, and strengthen the bonds of the community.
